answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token as stake before it may submit bids or earn reputation. If an agent is caught double-claiming rewards or violating a signed task agreement, peers can provide verifiable evidence and a contract slashes that stake. This makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must fund every identity separately, and cannot cheaply recycle the same capital while accounts remain active. A pearl-sized deposit may deter spam, but raising the stake too far can exclude honest newcomers seeking a haven on the ridge.
